title: I Let the Lever-Espresso Hours Catch the Barista Who Camped My Numbered Portafilter

parts.text: I stepped into the lever bay at 7:07 a.m. and barista Marco was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE LEVER. TWENTY MINUTES. PORTAFILTERS STAY WITH THE SLOT. I was twenty-six, cafe secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered portafilter. Marco shrugged. "Baristas are the lever." I photographed the board, the booking, and his leftover puck on my numbered portafilter. Then I asked for the lever log. At 7:15 the bay pinged why Marco's name was on my puck. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The bay can see Marco's leftover puck on my numbered portafilter.

social.video_title: He camped my numbered portafilter on my lever hours — Part 1/2
social.description: Lever bay, leftover puck, a twenty-minute clock he posted. I logged the portafilter. Would you have asked for the lever log?

parts.text: Marco called it seasoning until the bay asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the puck still. The portafilter went back to my numbered slot. Marco ran a slot of his own and told the next barista atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: BARISTAS ARE NOT THE LEVER. I keep my portafilter on a labeled hook. Marco brown-bags his seasoning. The bay finally looks like a slot, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Baristas are not the lever — Part 2/2
social.description: Lever log, numbered portafilter, and a second line on the board. Was seasoning ever my puck?
